children: is expanding manufacturing capacity for its new oral obesity treatment as Chief Executive David Ricks said the drug is gaining ground among patients starting GLP-1 pills.

Ricks told CNBC that Foundayo accounts for roughly one-third of new oral GLP-1 prescriptions, with its share continuing to rise. The company also expects to introduce the treatment in additional international markets over the coming months.

The comments came as Lilly broke ground on a $6.5 billion manufacturing facility in Houston. The site is expected to begin operations in 2030 and will produce Foundayo's active ingredient along with materials for other small-molecule medicines. Lilly said the project is part of a broader effort to expand U.S. pharmaceutical production.

Foundayo generated $98 million in second-quarter sales during its first three months on the U.S. market. Lilly is also seeking broader uses for the drug, including type 2 diabetes, with additional data expected later this year.
Medicare coverage for obesity treatments that began in July could also widen access to GLP-1 medicines, including Lilly's Foundayo and Zepbound.

title: Eli Lilly CEO Delivers Urgent Message on the Company's Next Big Weight-Loss Pill
